name: Rush Kingdom
species: Human kingdom with separately chartered allied peoples
leader_direction: The Golden King, followed by the canonical succession packages.
placement: Temperate Europe and North America, weighted toward plains, forest, hills, and rivers.
history_proposal: The crossing preserves the institutions of the Rush plains and the obligations of Selen, Hiloron, Kilinti, Huhun, and the island houses. The original causes of the Ainu disappearance and Einendil freezing remain unresolved.
starting_problem: A powerful army has arrived under a greedy ruler whose short-term bargains undermine the political settlement.
ai: Follow the full Rush political plan. High influence changes succession preparation, never the mandatory death or war.
asset_direction: Golden royal display against practical frontier equipment. Each late government has a distinct portrait and flag transition.
source_status: User-named identity with proposed gameplay and biography

name: Elves of the Magical Forest
species: Elves with protected Earth civilian communities
leader_direction: An elected forest envoy who must justify military action to a public assembly.
placement: Remote forest, mountain, and highland states, with low population density as a secondary weight.
history_proposal: The settlers carry forest law and a tradition of choosing their representatives. Their memories link the Magical Forest to the Magic Mountains and Dragon Mountain, without claiming that all magical peoples share one government.
starting_problem: The Earth state needs housing and supply, but unrestricted construction would damage the forests that make the colony viable.
ai: Prefer recognition and defense. Authorize intervention only for a real attacked partner or exposed dark threat, and keep a reserve at home.
asset_direction: Ancient living-wood armor, restrained silver fittings, and a distinct elected envoy. Dragons follow the separate Dragon Mountain military brief.
source_status: User-named identity with proposed gameplay and biography

name: Noris Desert Warriors
species: Humans with optional contracted frontier creatures
leader_direction: A caravan commander whose authority depends on keeping water and supply routes open.
placement: Dry states in North Africa, Arabia, Iran, Central Asia, Australia, and the Americas.
history_proposal: Noris remembers wells, caravan obligations, and the border between settled desert routes and the harsher southern territories. Departure followed a disputed decision to protect traders rather than serve every southern warlord.
starting_problem: Military mobility is strong, but the settlement must secure reliable supply and decide who can use its routes.
ai: Choose trade when routes are open, guardianship when neighbors are threatened, and conquest only after viable supply and a target have been prepared.
asset_direction: Practical layered desert clothing and camel equipment with a distinct Noris emblem. Avoid borrowing a real ethnic costume as proof of fictional identity.
source_status: User-named identity with proposed gameplay and biography

name: Dondor Brutes
species: Humans
leader_direction: A human war-captain selected through a military hierarchy, visibly distinct from an ogre or demon.
placement: Rough frontier states in the Middle East, Anatolia, Caucasus, Balkans, and North Africa.
history_proposal: Dondor carries a history of harsh frontier service near the Dark Forests and Blackton. Its soldiers remember negotiating with stronger beings without accepting that those beings should rule humans.
starting_problem: The host state cannot indefinitely support the military establishment through requisition alone, and the captains disagree over service to a dark patron.
ai: Negotiate from strength. Consider patronage when isolated or under threat, but compare the actual cost of subordination with independent war-making.
asset_direction: Heavy human armor, broad shields, and practical captured Earth equipment. The portrait must remain clearly human.
source_status: User-named identity with proposed gameplay and biography

name: Gunwaith Highland Clans
species: Human highland clans
leader_direction: A clan speaker who organized a joint crossing while promising that no clan would lose its own law.
placement: Scandinavia, Scotland, Alpine regions, the Rockies, Canada, and comparable highlands.
history_proposal: The clans remember the white northern lands of Gunwaith and the smaller inhabited approaches south of them. Their proposed departure dispute concerns winter stores and the right of one clan to close a shared mountain passage.
starting_problem: The settlement has defensible terrain but several competing local commands. Centralizing too quickly risks losing the scouts needed to defend the passes.
routes: Unlock cooperative pass defense and a northern league role. Clans retain local law and cannot be sold into a patron pact.
Gain a larger standing army and a direct conquest route after activation, at the cost of local resistance to foreign campaigns.
Keep a complete neutral route with civilian shelter, mountain defense, and paid allied logistics without compulsory global faction membership.

mission.label: Keep the winter passage open
mission.proof: Control the founding state, keep its supply route functioning, and deliver one support-equipment shipment to a named partner.
mission.success: A second highland mustering allotment and a permanent clan agreement.
mission.failure: The affected clan withdraws offensive service until a repaired route is held for 90 days.

actions: Commit five existing formations to a 90-day defense obligation, then unlock one replacement allotment.
A recorded dispute with one clan
Choose compensation or central enforcement. Compensation preserves the league route, enforcement strengthens the crown and loses local cooperation.
ai: Prefer confederation when a cooperative northern neighbor exists. Prefer centralization after repeated attacks. Never launch a warm-climate expedition while the home winter route is failing.
asset_direction: Highland stonework, winter cloaks, and clan-specific shields. Use Gunwaith geography from the North Earth sheet, not the Cold Lands yeti map.
source_status: User-named identity with proposed gameplay and biography

name: Girdon River Wardens
species: Humans
leader_direction: A river warden elected by settlement and bridge keepers.
placement: Forested river valleys and lake regions, with actual crossing infrastructure where available.
history_proposal: Girdon remembers the river, the northern forests, and the approaches to Buldor. Its proposed founding argument was whether a river authority could remain neutral when rival armies demanded exclusive passage. The goblin engineers are a contracted northern company, not a normal Rush population.
starting_problem: Control of bridges brings revenue and military value, but the new country must decide whether transit rules protect civilians or favor a patron.
routes: Create a joint rescue and repair service
Build a neutral transport and relief state with defensive engineers and enforceable access agreements.
Gain strong river defense and allied supply commitments. Deliberate demolitions require an actual military target and damage real infrastructure.
Grant one foreign partner privileged access
Accept or reject a dependent relationship
Receive construction and equipment support while risking political dependence. The final choice preserves independence at a real economic cost or accepts a subject contract.

mission.label: Deliver the river relief convoy
mission.proof: A named aid agreement, an open route, and the actual equipment shipment arrive.
mission.success: A durable rescue agreement and an additional engineer allotment.
mission.failure: The partner withdraws its transit guarantee and the failed aid receipt cannot be reused.

actions: A controlled or treaty-authorized damaged river state
Repair actual infrastructure and improve that partner relationship.
A live patron contract and a declared replacement supply route
End the privilege without deleting the partner's delivered buildings or equipment.
ai: Prioritize routes with an actual crossing and sufficient supply. Refuse rival military concessions that would violate an existing neutral charter.
asset_direction: River measuring poles, practical bridge gear, and forest uniforms. Separate warden and contracted goblin visual families.
source_status: User-named identity with proposed gameplay and biography

name: Keredr Villagers
species: Human rural settlers
leader_direction: A village delegate who brought the settlement rolls through the crossing.
placement: Productive plains, rural hills, and states with room for civilian development.
history_proposal: The settlers remember the rural region labeled Keredr Villagers on the West Earth sheet. Their proposed history centers on a local refusal to let distant military rulers requisition the next harvest.
starting_problem: They have a defensible community and little offensive power. Recognition and reliable allies matter more than a sudden empire.
routes: Integrate Earth residents through common citizenship
Build a friendly democratic colony with militia defense, refugee reception, and a Lost Cause option.
Limit foreign military use of the state
Remain neutral with a complete food, construction, and civil-defense route. Guarantees cannot contradict one another.
Return authority or retain emergency rule
Gain a stronger militia during a real threat, then choose a constitutional return or an authoritarian protectorate.

mission.label: Complete the first civil settlement
mission.proof: Deliver housing construction, keep civilian reception within capacity, and preserve a lawful resident policy.
mission.success: A civilian-capacity improvement and integrated Earth volunteer recruitment.
mission.failure: Local communities withhold recruitment until reception or housing is repaired.

actions: 50 PP and two civilian factories for 90 days
A valid Migration request and a safe destination
Accept the actual cohort through the shared transfer owner and gain a durable aid relationship.
An actual war or a threatened border with a hostile activated colony
Raise five militia formations from the admitted human pool, with demobilization obligations after the threat.
ai: Prefer recognition, construction, and guarantees. Do not accept a dark patron merely because it offers equipment while a safe neutral or good partner exists.
asset_direction: Village records, practical rural militia clothing, and an elected civilian portrait. Keep the state identity modest rather than turning it into a royal court.
source_status: User-named identity with proposed gameplay and biography

name: Enhesis River Islanders
species: Humans and locally admitted island communities
leader_direction: A pilot-captain selected by river and harbor delegates.
placement: Islands, deltas, archipelagos, and coastal states with a real port.
history_proposal: Enhesis remembers the waterways shared with Rono, Howan, and the nearby island settlements. The proposed crossing followed a dispute over whether island pilots should carry armed clients through neutral waters.
starting_problem: The colony needs maritime trade but must decide which military passengers it is willing to carry.
routes: Create a durable neutral shipping state with rescue missions and paid transport contracts.
Build a regional naval compact and a natural route into the Lost Cause when members are threatened.
Gain raiding power after activation, but lose neutral protection and risk war with former clients.

mission.label: Keep an evacuation passage safe
mission.proof: A named civilian convoy route remains open and its actual survivors reach the receiving state.
mission.success: A rescue compact and additional marine replacement capacity.
mission.failure: The loss is recorded by the transport owner, and the colony must repair its damaged neutrality or guarantee.

actions: A valid receiving partner and safe port pair
Commit transport to one evacuation or aid operation.
An exposed breach of a current neutral transport agreement
Hold the contract force until a negotiated release, or cancel the contract and accept the diplomatic consequences.
ai: Favor neutrality while ports are safe. Join collective defense after attacks on shipping. Refuse troop transport that would silently enter an offensive war.
asset_direction: River craft, harbor pilot insignia, and island marine equipment. The map crop must retain Enhesis and nearby waterways.
source_status: User-named identity with proposed gameplay and biography

name: Rush Island Confederacy
species: Rush human island houses
leader_direction: A rotating house captain, replaced by a named royal governor only after a lawful crown agreement.
placement: Ocean islands, Britain, Japan, the Caribbean, Indonesia, and other defensible maritime states.
history_proposal: The houses preserve memories of Rush, Asgard, Hould, Faber, and Tint and their disputes over continental obligations. Their crossing can establish a maritime base independent of the Golden King.
starting_problem: The houses want mutual protection but disagree over whether the mainland crown can command their ships.
routes: Choose constitutional loyalty or royal monopoly
Provide actual ships and marines to Rush, then participate in its succession according to the charter.
Remain a complete neutral or Lost Cause naval country with shared defense and competitive trade.
Shelter a defeated good Rush camp
Become a surviving good Rush successor after Afrit's usurpation, without creating another Golden King or Einendil.

mission.label: Honor the house naval pledge
mission.proof: A committed fleet or marine contingent supports the named defense operation and returns with a valid service receipt.
mission.success: A house agreement and later fleet modernization access.
mission.failure: The affected house withdraws its next contribution and disputes central command.

actions: A functioning port and a ratified naval charter
Release the finite charter fleet or replacement tranche, never a new fleet on every use.
A defeated good Rush institution and valid civilian reception
Admit the surviving people and political claim without copying their destroyed armies.
ai: Compare actual Rush conduct, not only shared origin. Resist Afrit unless the house was separately compromised or conquered.
asset_direction: Five coherent house motifs within one maritime identity. Route flags distinguish royal service, free confederacy, and lawful exile without palette-swap variants.
source_status: User-named identity with proposed gameplay and biography

name: Coldor Yeti Clans
species: Yetis
leader_direction: A winter assembly speaker with a scarred expedition staff and a practical duty to feed the clans.
placement: Arctic, tundra, snowy mountain, Siberian, Canadian, Alaskan, and Greenland states.
history_proposal: Coldor remembers the Frozen Lands of Coldor and routes toward the Yeti Lands. Its proposed migration split was between clans seeking shelter and chiefs seeking a new cold kingdom.
starting_problem: Warm seasons and poor replacement access can defeat the colony even when its winter troops are strong.
routes: Remain defensive, join a friendly northern league, and shelter other cold peoples without compulsory conquest.
Permit limited cold-region conquest after activation. Warm campaigns retain their logistical penalties.
Exchange envoys with the later yeti kingdom
Ratify equal union or remain allied
Create a substantive yeti political union without awarding either side another starting army.

mission.label: Survive the first warm season
mission.proof: Maintain supply, complete an adaptation program, and keep a functioning cold reserve at home.
mission.success: Reduce the worst outside-climate penalty and unlock a second finite yeti allotment.
mission.failure: Replacement throughput falls until the settlement has completed a 90-day supply repair.

actions: A controlled cold state and unused reserve commitment
Assign a limited yeti reserve to the home defense.
A non-hostile partner able to deliver the named shipment
Exchange a defensive obligation for sustained supplies.
ai: Refuse deep hot-climate offensives while adaptation is incomplete. Prefer Worldond union only when that ruler respects clan autonomy.
asset_direction: Distinct fur, posture, and winter equipment. Do not use an enlarged human soldier model.
source_status: User-named identity with proposed gameplay and biography

name: Goodin Sunfolk
species: Humans or near-human sunfolk, with exact physiology left to canon review
leader_direction: A civic envoy responsible for warm-coast trade and the protection of guests.
placement: Warm coasts, Mediterranean states, India, Southeast Asia, and Central America.
history_proposal: Goodin remembers its place near the Sea of Gods and the larger Sunhot societies. The proposed colony began as a civilian expedition that expected trade rather than a war against Earth.
starting_problem: A friendly posture attracts displaced people faster than the small country can house them.
routes: Build integration, light defense, and a strong Lost Cause alignment.
Establish contact with a Sunhot arrival
Retain civilian independence under military protection
Receive limited elite help after actual Sunhot availability, without pretending the patron exists at baseline.
Create a trading and relief role that remains viable outside the three factions until threatened.

mission.label: House the arriving guests
mission.proof: Deliver a real reception project and complete one valid integration or onward-resettlement outcome.
mission.success: More civilian capacity and a trusted civil-partner relationship.
mission.failure: Overcrowding remains visible and blocks new voluntary admissions until repaired.

actions: A valid safe state with an admitted construction project
Increase real reception capacity through the shared system.
A living friendly Sunhot country and a real threatened aid route
Ask for one limited escort commitment, which Sunhot may refuse if unable to defend its own people.
ai: Prioritize reception and supply. Do not open more admissions when the shared reception system says the destination is unsafe.
asset_direction: Warm civic colors, practical light infantry, and a calm civilian envoy. Keep Goodin distinct from the towering Sunhot elf unit family.
source_status: User-named identity with proposed gameplay and biography

name: Buldor Stone Companies
species: Human engineering and heavy-infantry companies
leader_direction: A company marshal elected by foremen and veteran officers.
placement: Hills, mineral regions, fortified industrial states, and mountain approaches.
history_proposal: Buldor remembers stone companies working between mountain roads and defended settlements. The proposed departure followed a contract dispute over whether a patron could claim ownership of the companies themselves.
starting_problem: The colony needs contracts to sustain its workshops, but repeated service to one patron can cost its independence.
routes: Maintain a neutral mercenary and reconstruction country with enforceable withdrawal conditions.
Secure a mineral and supply base
Create a strong fortified state whose work supports allies and civilians.
Choose subject status or a costly buyout
Gain faster industrial development while preserving a real late independence decision.

mission.label: Finish the contracted defense works
mission.proof: Complete the agreed actual buildings in the named state and provide its promised garrison or repair service.
mission.success: Payment, a trusted-contract receipt, and a heavy-company replacement allotment.
mission.failure: Forfeit the unearned payment and open a contract dispute instead of generating free resources.

actions: 50 PP and two civilian factories for 180 days
A willing partner, legal construction access, and a specific target state
Commit to actual defensive construction with a fixed payment and withdrawal clause.
An active concession and a replacement supply agreement
End dependence while retaining completed paid-for facilities and losing future patron shipments.
ai: Compare supply access and the likelihood of completing the contract. Never accept simultaneous contracts requiring the same company in incompatible wars.
asset_direction: Heavy tools, stone-work motifs, and disciplined shield infantry. Company symbols must remain readable without tiny written contract text.
source_status: User-named identity with proposed gameplay and biography

name: Bloody Forest Orc March
species: Independent orcs
leader_direction: An orc frontier chief who treats promises as personal obligations, not automatic loyalty to Rush.
placement: Temperate forest frontiers and wooded mountain borders in Europe or North America.
history_proposal: The March remembers the Bloody Forest and hostile dealings with the wider Rush region. Its proposed crossing was a break with a chief who wanted to sell the clan to a dark patron.
starting_problem: The clan is powerful enough to raid but too small to survive endless wars with every neighbor.
routes: Remain an independent or mercenary orc country with limited regional ambitions.
Join Afrit or Volgan through actual subordination and its costs, not species alone.
Receive aid after a real betrayal or threat
Ratify a rare alliance with a good Rush government
Open an exceptional Lost Cause route. It requires prior events and never becomes the default Rush recruitment path.

mission.label: Keep the frontier oath
mission.proof: Honor the named non-aggression and civilian-protection terms while holding the border.
mission.success: A durable independence agreement and access to the exceptional good alliance when other conditions hold.
mission.failure: The oath is recorded as broken and the rare route closes for that political generation.

actions: A legal contract with a reachable front
Commit existing riders for 90 days with an explicit return condition.
Retain the host and risk the patron's coercion, opening an anti-patron defense route.
ai: Default to independence, mercenary service, or hostile expansion. Rare good alignment requires actual aid and a completed oath, never a flat friendly-ideology weight.
asset_direction: Forest orc armor and visibly distinct warg riders. Use Rush Land geography without presenting the March as a normal Rush dominion.
source_status: User-named identity with proposed gameplay and biography

name: Stone Forest Goblin League
species: Independent goblins
leader_direction: A workshop delegate chosen by tunnel and salvage crews.
placement: Hills, forests, mountain passes, and damaged industrial states.
history_proposal: The League remembers Stone Forest workshops and the need to bargain with larger armies. The proposed crossing followed a dispute over whether tunnel maps should be sold to a single ruler.
starting_problem: Its technical skills make it valuable, but selling the same secret twice can turn every neighbor hostile.
routes: Create a useful neutral country whose income and army depend on completed projects.
Choose a dark patron or independent sabotage
Open sabotage and war production after activation, with exposure and counterintelligence risks.
Permit a rare friendly route without making goblins an ordinary Rush population.

mission.label: Complete the salvage commission
mission.proof: A real damaged or captured equipment lot is assigned, repaired, and delivered to its recorded client.
mission.success: Payment and one engineer reinforcement allotment.
mission.failure: Lose the unpaid balance and retain responsibility for any diverted equipment.

actions: A willing client and an actual repairable lot
Convert the recorded salvage once, not a percentage of an unlimited abstract stockpile.
A proven exposure or betrayal receipt
Withdraw access and defend the affected state, accepting the client's response.
ai: Prefer contracts it can complete. Do not sell incompatible exclusive access to enemies without deliberately choosing the risky hidden-industry route.
asset_direction: Compact goblin engineers, tunnel tools, and recovered machinery. The civil and sabotage paths need distinct icon motifs, not a renamed human engineer counter.
source_status: User-named identity with proposed gameplay and biography

name: Lothord Fog Trollholds
species: Northern trolls
leader_direction: A pass-keeper whose authority rests on protecting several small holds.
placement: Foggy highlands, northern coasts, remote hills, and mountains.
history_proposal: The Trollholds remember the Lothord Fog Mountains and disputes over who could cross them in winter. Their proposed departure followed the collapse of an old toll agreement with neighboring rulers.
starting_problem: The army is extremely strong at home but slow, scarce, and vulnerable to being committed too far away.
routes: Remain neutral and defensively valuable in a northern league.
Expand along a limited mountain corridor
Open a regional expansion route based on actual connected states after activation.
Commit one host under a written obligation
Gain support with a real loss of independence and a difficult revolt option.

mission.label: Hold the agreed pass
mission.proof: Keep a named controlled mountain state supplied and honor its passage agreement.
mission.success: A second replacement allotment and stronger northern diplomatic ties.
mission.failure: The client withdraws support and the affected hold refuses another distant deployment.

actions: A threatened mountain state and unused troll allotment
Assign the real host to a 90-day defense commitment.
A current transit partner and a recorded dispute
Choose a paid neutral settlement or an explicit coercive demand that can provoke war.
ai: Value defensible terrain and sustainable supply over nominal territorial size. Avoid tropical campaigns without a paid and viable logistics agreement.
asset_direction: Heavy fog-weathered trolls with local stone equipment. Keep them distinct from frost trolls and the shadowed Endless host.
source_status: User-named identity with proposed gameplay and biography

name: Eye Mountain Ogreholds
species: Northern ogres
leader_direction: A clan judge whose personal authority must survive disputes among shock-force chiefs.
placement: Mountain states, isolated uplands, and mineral regions.
history_proposal: The Ogreholds remember the Eye Mountains and the need to negotiate access to mineral and trade routes. Their proposed crossing split the clans between service contracts and a new mountain kingdom.
starting_problem: Chiefs want raids, while the settlement needs roads, supplies, and a lawful division of contracts.
routes: Create a neutral or defensive mercenary state with finite ogre deployments.
Permit regional conquest after activation, with clan disputes when campaigns fail.
Allow a northern good route through conduct. It does not make the Ogreholds a Rush dominion.

mission.label: Deliver the mountain service
mission.proof: A named host completes a reachable defense or siege contract without abandoning the home supply route.
mission.success: Payment and a clan agreement for another finite host.
mission.failure: A chief contests the ruler and blocks new offensive contracts until arbitration.

actions: A recorded failed or competing contract
Preserve the service council or strengthen a single ruler with a corresponding political cost.
Commit the existing support force to repair and transport duties for 90 days.
ai: Prefer short, reachable contracts. Choose an anti-demon compact only after an actual coercive threat and successful protection pledge.
asset_direction: Broad ogre bodies, heavy carrying frames, and mountain weapons. Do not reuse Hiloron giant anatomy or political symbols.
source_status: User-named identity with proposed gameplay and biography

name: Worshipdom of Afrit
species: Human servants, demons, and individually corrupted peoples
leader_direction: Afrit. The same unique character later holds the Rush crown if his claim succeeds.
placement: Broad placement with extra weight for politically unstable, accessible states. The exact homeland map is not established by the brief.
history_proposal: Afrit begins as the weaker dark power and works through worship, bargains, compromised rulers, and captured institutions. His rule is separate from Volgan's ancient Dead Lands realm.
starting_problem: Direct conquest against Volgan is initially unrealistic. The valuable opportunity is Rush and the institutions that can be captured through its succession.
ai: Prioritize influence, defensible territory, and a viable Rush claim. Do not start a war with Volgan merely because both are evil.
asset_direction: Afrit requires a Worshipdom portrait and a distinct King of Rush transformation. His exact homeland map remains an art-source question.
source_status: User-named identity with proposed gameplay and biography

name: Shachihata Demons
species: Very large demons with a small supporting settlement
leader_direction: A demon host-leader whose size and armor must be clearly different from a human warlord.
placement: East and Southeast Asia, volcanic states, mountains, and comparable warm regions.
history_proposal: The host remembers Shachihata and the difficult southern borderlands. Its proposed crossing argument concerns whether service to another power protects its people or consumes them.
starting_problem: The army is extremely powerful but small, and the colony must secure food, shelter, and replacements before choosing a patron.
ai: Remain neutral during provisioning. Compare the actual protection and obligations offered by Afrit and Volgan, and preserve an independent option.
asset_direction: Very large bodies, specially built equipment, and architecture visibly too small for the newcomers. No generic red human demon reskin.
source_status: User-named identity with proposed gameplay and biography

name: Pulundur Dark-Sea Raiders
species: Sea orcs and associated human crews
leader_direction: A fleet captain who escaped an exclusive levy from a stronger dark ruler.
placement: Ports, islands, narrow seas, and isolated coasts.
history_proposal: Pulundur remembers the Dark Sea and the competition between coastal rulers who demanded ships without paying crews. Its proposed crossing preserved a fleet community whose loyalty is to its captains before any distant dark throne.
starting_problem: A raiding fleet needs repair facilities and safe buyers. Uncontrolled attacks can close every harbor the colony needs.
routes: Remain neutral or selectively hostile with contracts that do not automatically serve Afrit.
Attack a named enemy supply route
Negotiate autonomy or accept cult control
Provide a real naval arm for The Ashen Throne, with a revolt path if the charter is broken.
Build a chain of occupied ports
Expand only after activation and with actual transport and supply proof. Captured harbors create garrison and repair obligations.

mission.label: Return the contracted fleet
mission.proof: Complete one reachable naval-support contract and return the committed ships or surviving crews to a valid port.
mission.success: Payment, a repair agreement, and a limited marine replacement allotment.
mission.failure: Losses remain real and the captains can refuse another patron contract.

actions: A named client, valid target, and activated external policy
Commit to a particular campaign instead of unrestricted attacks on all trade.
A controlled damaged port or a willing treaty partner
Repair actual port capacity and bind the access agreement.
ai: Never raid a state solely because it is coastal. Prefer reachable targets with a repair port and avoid contracts against its own guaranteed partner.
asset_direction: Dark-sea ship crews, boarding gear, and a distinctive sea-orc model. News uses Pulundur and the Dark Sea, not the Dead Lands.
source_status: User-named identity with proposed gameplay and biography

name: Goldoroth Ash Host
species: Human and mixed ash-warrior companies, distinct from the ogre kingdom
leader_direction: A campaign marshal whose authority comes from keeping ash-frontier troops supplied.
placement: Volcanic, dry mountain, desert, and devastated states.
history_proposal: The Ash Host remembers the Goldoroth frontier and military service near the Dark Gate. Its proposed break with the homeland followed a dispute over whether the host could refuse a ruinous campaign.
starting_problem: The host is good at fighting in devastated terrain but cannot sustain an economy by continuing to devastate every conquered state.
routes: Remain independent with paid siege service and a reconstruction route.
Bind the command to the Ashen Throne
Gain corruption-linked support and a clear anti-Volgan role without inheriting the ogre kingdom.
Choose reconstruction or permanent military extraction
Open regional conquest with meaningful civilian and economic consequences.

mission.proof: Repair actual industry and supply in the founding or acquired frontier state without destroying the settlement workforce.
mission.success: Permanent workshop capacity and one heavy replacement allotment.
mission.failure: Offensive reinforcements remain restricted and a patron can demand a costly exclusive contract.

actions: A reachable named fortification target and lawful war contract
Commit existing ash troops for 90 days.
A live patron demand that would damage a controlled settlement
Preserve the workforce and lose the offered patron shipment.
ai: Prefer reconstruction when the home economy is weak. An Afrit affinity changes diplomatic preference but does not create automatic obedience.
asset_direction: Ash-weathered human and mixed troops with practical protective equipment. Keep them visibly and mechanically separate from Goldoroth ogres.

name: Titanos Ice Giants
species: Ice giants
leader_direction: An expedition elder who has brought only a small part of the Titanos host.

history_proposal: Titanos remembers the northern ice and the routes between the frozen countries. The proposed colony is a limited expedition, not the migration of every giant in Titanos.

routes: Remain neutral or join a defensive cold league.
Intervene against a demonstrated dark threat
Use overwhelming but limited force in defense, with no automatic universal good alignment.
Permit conquest after activation while making distant warm campaigns expensive and slow.

mission.label: Preserve the expedition host
mission.proof: Keep a viable supplied giant force and complete the cold sanctuary works.
mission.success: One additional finite giant replacement tranche and an accepted sanctuary.
mission.failure: The homeland refuses further offensive musters until the supply failure is repaired.

actions: A secure crossing and an unused Titanos allotment
Release the small admitted giant force after its training period.
Commit to defend that specific settlement for 180 days.
ai: Keep a home reserve and avoid splitting the entire giant force among distant fronts. Prefer protection over conquest when the colony is treated well.

name: Mushroom Forest Mycids
species: Fungal beings
leader_direction: A spore-speaker represented by one coherent fictional organism or governing cluster.
placement: Wet forests, swamps, jungle, and remote humid states.
history_proposal: The mycids remember the Mushroom Forest and its boundary with the Magical Forest. Their proposed crossing followed a dispute over whether expanding the living forest justified entering another people's settlements.
starting_problem: The colony needs a protected habitat, but uncontrolled expansion can damage Earth communities and turn friendly elves against it.

Extend the habitat through agreement or war
Expand only through real state ownership and a declared policy. A state modifier represents growth without claiming the engine changed terrain.
Bind the spore guard to a patron
Choose submission or a costly cleansing
Provide a distinct corrupted military route with lasting political consequences.

mission.proof: Keep the declared habitat within the admitted state and complete any required resident agreement or safe movement.
mission.success: Defensive growth benefits and a second mycid allotment.
mission.failure: A neighboring community dispute and reduced recognition until the boundary is repaired.

Create the bounded habitat effect and its exact state record.
A proven corrupted state and a valid friendly cleansing route
Remove that specific binding over 180 days, losing its military benefit while restoring independence.
ai: Prefer wet habitat and bounded defense. Do not treat every forest as already colonized or spread effects through an unbounded world scan.

name: Zhen Hills Arcanists
species: Human or near-human arcanists and their attendants
leader_direction: A collegiate examiner responsible for controlling dangerous projects.
placement: Hills, mountain basins, and remote inland states.
history_proposal: The arcanists remember the Zhen Hills and the neighboring magical regions. Their proposed departure dispute concerned who could authorize a project whose failure would affect people outside the college.
starting_problem: Their projects can solve real military and supply problems, but outside patrons want control of the research and its people.
routes: Build a neutral or good specialist state with support formations and verified civilian projects.
Use limited intervention to secure research sites
Create an independent power with strong specialist support and political responsibility for failures.
